'''''Lonicera fragrantissima''''' is a species of flowering plant in the honeysuckle family [[Caprifoliaceae]], known by the common names '''winter-flowering honeysuckle''',<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/68665/Lonicera-fragrantissima/Details | title = ''Lonicera fragrantissima'' | publisher = [[Royal Horticultural Society]] | access-date = 3 March 2021}}</ref>  '''fragrant honeysuckle''',<ref name = GRIN>{{GRIN}}</ref> '''kiss-me-at-the-gate''',<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/kiss-me-at-the-gate | title = Kiss-me-at-the-gate | publisher = Merriam-Webster | access-date = 3 March 2021}}</ref> and '''sweet breath of spring'''.<ref>{{EOL}}</ref> It is native to China and has been an [[introduced species]] to other parts of the world.  It was brought to the attention of western gardeners by Scottish plant hunter [[Robert Fortune]], who was [[plant collecting|plant hunting]] in China for the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]. Fortune introduced ''Lonicera fragrantissima'' to England in 1845, and a few years later it was introduced to the United States. In 1853 the editor of American gardening magazine ''The Horticulturist'' wrote that the previous year he had been sent a specimen from a plant that had been flowering in the gardens of [[Hatfield House]], the Marquess of Salisbury's stately home in Hertfordshire.  The first mention of a specimen for commercial sale in an American plant catalogue is in 1860.<ref name=Cothran>{{cite book | last = Cothran | first = James R.  | title = Gardens and historic plants of the antebellum South  | publisher = University of South Carolina Press| date = 2003  | pages = 219  | url = https://books.google.com/books?id=s8OcSmOKeCkC&q=lonicera+fragrantissima+robert+fortune&pg=PA219}}</ref>

The honeysuckle is used as an [[ornamental plant]] for its fragrant flowers. In some parts of the world, where conditions are right, when it moves out of cultivation and takes hold in the wild, it can become an [[invasive species|invasive]] weed.<ref name=feis>Munger, Gregory T. (2005). [http://www.fs.fed.us/database/feis/plants/shrub/lonspp/all.html ''Lonicera'' spp.] In: Fire Effects Information System, [Online]. U.S. Department of Agriculture, Forest Service, Rocky Mountain Research Station, Fire Sciences Laboratory. Retrieved January 18, 2012.</ref>

This [[honeysuckle]], a species of "bush honeysuckle", is a [[shrub]] usually growing {{convert|1|to|3|m|ft}} tall, sometimes reaching a maximum height around {{convert|4.6|m|ft}}. When mature it is a bushy tangle of slender, spreading branches. The leaves are up to {{convert|9|cm|in}} long by {{convert|4.5|cm|in}} wide. The flowers, borne in pairs, are each about {{convert|1|cm|in}} long.<ref name=feis/> They are white to "creamy white" in color.<ref name=mobot>[http://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/gardens-gardening/your-garden/plant-finder/plant-details/kc/d970/lonicera-fragrantissima.aspx ''Lonicera fragrantissima''.] Missouri Botanical Garden. Retrieved January 18, 2012.</ref> They are very fragrant, with a "lemony" scent.<ref name=mobot/> The fruit is a red [[Berry (botany)|berry]] up to a centimeter wide.<ref name=feis/><ref name=mobot/> The seeds are [[seed dispersal|dispersed]] by animals that eat the fruits. The seeds must be [[Stratification (botany)|stratified]] before they will [[germination|germinate]].<ref name=feis/>

This plant, considered a "harbinger of spring",<ref name=mobot/> is grown for ornamental purposes and as a [[hedge]]. It can be found growing in parts of the eastern United States from [[Ohio]] to [[New York (state)|New York]] to the southeastern states where it is an introduced species. It has also been observed in [[Utah]].<ref name=feis/>
